title: Danny Boyle Shares Why He Used AI for Maggie Thatcher in ‘Ink’ – Without Asking Her Estate
key_facts: Director Danny Boyle spoke at the 70th BFI London Film Festival on Friday 9 Oct 2026, in a talk with Puck's Matt Belloni.
His film Ink traces Rupert Murdoch's rise on Fleet Street and takeover of the tabloid The Sun.
The team hired an impersonator to play Margaret Thatcher, then used AI to put Thatcher's face on her.
Boyle said he declined to ask Thatcher's estate for permission and does not think estates should control ideas in art about a person's influence.
He said AI was used 'very sparingly' and carefully so it did not replace anyone.
He also warned that tech giants controlling platforms, with AI replacing journalists, could affect whether journalists can hold power to account.
quote_evidence: “I got to be honest, I declined to ask the estate for permission to do that.
“It’s a part of the toolbox that the visual effects companies use now,” the creative offered.
The Ink team did, however, use AI to recreate late U.K. Prime Minister Margaret “Maggie” Thatcher’s face.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows how filmmakers are using AI to recreate real people's faces and how they view consent.
notes: Boyle's own account at a public event, reported by one outlet. No legal ruling or estate response is reported.
